album: Presenting Thad Jones/Mel Lewis and the Jazz Orchestra
label: Solid State
rationale: The founding document of the modern jazz big band after Basie. The orchestra's first studio album, cut over three days in May 1966 at A&R Studios for Solid State, and the record that established the book and the personnel that held Monday nights at the Village Vanguard for decades [S2, S3, S7] (obs). Session gravity is the strongest case: Thad Jones (flugelhorn), Mel Lewis (drums), Hank Jones (piano), Pepper Adams (baritone), Bob Brookmeyer and Tom McIntosh (trombones), Richard Davis (bass), Jerome Richardson, Jerry Dodgion, Joe Farrell and Eddie Daniels in the reeds — most of them already in this canon on other records, assembled as a working band rather than a pickup date [S1, S2, S3] (obs). Lineage: the arranger's band — Jones, Brookmeyer and McIntosh charts — is the direct continuation of the Basie and Ellington big-band tradition already represented here, and it is the line that runs to the Vanguard Jazz Orchestra and to every working jazz orchestra since [S1, S2] (inf). Defining statement: 'A B C Blues' (12:53), 'Mean What You Say' and 'Three and One' are the book's signature pieces, and the album is where they were first recorded [S1, S2, S3] (obs). It still plays: the band swings from the first bar of 'Once Around', and the solo order — Adams, Hank Jones, Brookmeyer, Farrell, Daniels, Thad — is the point of the record [S1] (inf). Honest counterweight: the recorded-profile sources are thinner than a consensus-core case would want — AllMusic rates it 3/5 (S2's review table, S1), and no Penguin Crown, Hall of Fame or poll placement was found in the sources consulted, so the case rests on lineage and session gravity, not on consensus (obs). Scope note: recorded 4–6 May 1966, released 1966 — squarely inside the 1945–1985 window; style code hard-bop follows AllMusic's own classification of the record [S1] (obs).

personnel_record.studio: A & R Studios, New York City

personnel.name: Bob Brookmeyer
personnel.notes: Valve trombone per AllMusic review (S1); listed as trombone by S2/S3. Also arranger of 'Willow Weep for Me' and 'A B C Blues' (S3).

personnel.name: Tom McIntosh
personnel.notes: Trombone section; composer/arranger of 'Balanced Scales = Justice' (S3).

personnel.name: Cliff Heather
personnel.notes: Mosaic sessionography lists bass trombone (S3); Wikipedia lists simply 'trombone' (S2). Recorded as bass trombone with epistemic unk.

personnel.name: Jerome Richardson
personnel.notes: Reed section; doublings per S3: soprano saxophone, alto saxophone, flute, clarinet, bass clarinet.

personnel.name: Jerry Dodgion
personnel.notes: Reed section; doublings per S3: alto saxophone, flute, clarinet.

personnel.name: Joe Farrell
personnel.notes: Reed section; doublings per S3: tenor saxophone, flute, clarinet.

personnel.name: Eddie Daniels
personnel.notes: Reed section; doublings per S3: tenor saxophone, clarinet, bass clarinet.

personnel_record.notes: Three sessions: 4 May 1966 — 'A B C Blues' (tk 4); 'Kids Are Pretty People' from the same date was issued only on the Mosaic box, not on SS-18003. 5 May — 'Once Around' (tk 8), 'Don't Ever Leave Me' (tk 12). 6 May — 'Three in One' (tk 7), 'Balanced Scales = Justice' (tk 4), 'Willow Weep for Me' (tk 13), 'Mean What You Say' (tk 6) [S3]. The track printed as 'Three in One' is properly 'Three and One' — the cover title is an error, confirmed on the original parts [S2]. Arrangements: Thad Jones except 'Willow Weep for Me' and 'A B C Blues' (Bob Brookmeyer) and 'Balanced Scales = Justice' (Tom McIntosh) [S3]. Assistant producer Manny Albam [S3]. Engineers per the Mosaic discography are assigned by session group: Phil Ramone for the May 1966 sessions [S3, S7]. Cliff Heather's instrument conflicts between sources — bass trombone in S3, trombone in S2 — recorded as bass trombone with epistemic unk. Wikipedia lists 16 players without Reed doublings; the doublings in each personnel note come from S3 (Bill Kirchner's research of the original scores).

ballot.album: Thad Jones & Mel Lewis — Presenting Thad Jones/Mel Lewis and the Jazz Orchestra (1966)
ballot.case_for: This is the debut studio document of the Thad Jones/Mel Lewis Orchestra, whose Village Vanguard residency and continuing legacy as the Vanguard Jazz Orchestra make it a defining institution in modern big-band jazz. Its signature repertoire and concentrated roster—including Thad Jones, Mel Lewis, Hank Jones, Pepper Adams, Bob Brookmeyer, and Richard Davis—give it unusually strong defining-statement, lineage, and session-gravity claims (S1, S2, S3).
ballot.case_against: The album’s critical-consensus signal is comparatively weak: AllMusic rates it 3/5, and the dossier found no Penguin Guide, Hall of Fame, or poll placement for this specific LP (S1; dossier research). Its historical importance may attach more to the orchestra and Vanguard residency than to this studio album, while later statements such as Consummation may be stronger artistic showcases; the dossier’s critical sourcing is also thinner than its discographical documentation.
ballot.recommendation: John should give it strong consideration as the foundational modern-big-band statement, while weighing its thin album-specific consensus and competition from the orchestra’s later work.
